section.title: The derivative as a function
section.p: The derivative at a specific point gives the slope of one tangent line. By letting the evaluation point vary across the domain, the derivative becomes an entirely new function f' mapping each x to the tangent slope at (x, f(x)).

subsection.title: From one tangent slope to many

subsection.title: Reading f' from the graph of f

table.title: Connecting geometry of f with values of f'

subsection.title: Reading f from the graph of f'
subsection.p: Sign analysis of f' reconstructs the qualitative behavior of f: positive f' indicates growth, negative f' indicates decline, and roots of f' indicate candidate local extrema.

warning.title: The derivative forgets constants
warning.p: Vertical shifts preserve slopes: \frac{d}{dx}(f(x)+C) = f'(x). Knowing f' determines f only up to an additive constant C.
